title: Network Timing and Process State Monitoring for IoT Energy Systems: An Evaluation with Data4Cyber
content: Integrity attacks on IoT energy systems can alter measurements, commands, or operating context through traffic that looks syntactically ordinary, so the choice of monitoring layer is a practical security question. This study compares traffic-timing, process-measurement, and operating-context evidence, together with a paired state-of-charge (SoC) reference residual, on the Data4Cyber v4 distribution-energy testbed. Isolation Forest models were fitted to benign S0 data, calibrated on a later chronological segment, and tested on eight attack recordings. At the 5% calibration quantile, family-balanced recall was 2.0% for packet timing, 44.8% for process measurements, and 23.3% for process plus context, at false-positive rates of 5.9%, 33.5%, and 10.9%. Ranking quality was weak, with family-balanced ROC-AUC between 0.54 and 0.57. The SoC residual threshold detected 85.2% of S4 attack rows at 5.9% benign false alarms and 49.7% of S5 rows. CUSUM reduced alarm episodes in some runs but had mixed effects on recall and false alarms. The packet-label audit found zero attack-labeled packets in S6 and S7, although the process labels mark attack-active intervals. All results come from one testbed recording per scenario and do not establish campaign-level generalization or robustness to adaptive attacks.
